courses.subject: LING
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: How Reading Works: Language, Cognition, and Literacy
courses.description: How do we go from looking at symbols on a page or screen to understanding the writer's message? How do children learn to read, and what ways of teaching reading best promote success for all students? We will explore these questions through analysis of language and writing structure and discussion of research data. Your final project will address a real-world question about reading, literacy, or reading education from the perspective of language and cognition.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Language in the U.S.A
courses.description: The linguistic landscape of the United States in historical and contemporary perspective: American English dialects, language maintenance and shift among Native American and immigrant groups, language politics and policy.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Language
courses.description: Introduction to the formal analysis of human language, including sounds, words, sentences, and language meaning, plus child language acquisition, language change over time, social attitudes toward language, and similarities and differences among languages. Other topics may include writing systems, animal communication, and language analysis by computers. Honors version available.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Linguistic Anthropology
courses.description: An introduction to linguistic anthropology and anthropological linguistics. The course approaches the complex interconnections between language, culture, and cognition; theoretical approaches employed during the past century (structuralism, functionalism, ethnoscience, universalism, linguistic relativity); common case studies (spatial language, colors, classifiers, deixis); verbal art (orality, literacy), linguistic ideology; and ethnolinguistic vitality.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language, Communication, and Human and Animal Minds
courses.description: An examination of the differences between natural human languages and other communication systems. Includes a philosophical inquiry into how languages relate to the world and the mind. Honors version available.

source.text: LING 145. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER. | PHIL 145 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Exploring the World's Languages
courses.description: Students develop an understanding of and appreciation for the diverse range of human languages across the planet, as well as the uniformity that underlies them. Topics include history, classification, and linguistic properties of the world's languages.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Phonology
courses.description: Description and analysis of sound systems of languages around the world. Introduction to formal phonological models, argumentation, and hypothesis testing. Students may not receive credit for both LING 200 and LING 523 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Syntax
courses.description: Introduction to the representational units and computational principles that underlie word order patterns in language. The course covers key discoveries and theories of generative approaches to syntax, in which grammars consist of formally defined rules and operations that generate grammatical sentences. Students may not receive credit for both LING 201 and LING 530 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Linguistic Variation and Language Change
courses.description: Introduction to the analysis and description of language change, relationships among languages, and types of linguistic structure. Students may not receive credit for both LING 202 and LING 525 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Acquisition and Development
courses.description: Provides an introduction to first-language acquisition, focusing on the acquisition of phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics, as well as on the social context of language acquisition and issues of atypical language development. Students may not receive credit for both LING 203 and LING 528 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: The Psychology of Language Learning Motivation: Why We Keep Going (or Give Up)
courses.description: Why do some people fall in love with language learning while others stop after 'hello'? This course explores the psychology of motivation and the factors that shape language learning, including emotion, identity, and educational context. Through global case studies, students investigate how these forces influence persistence and success. Coursework emphasizes hands-on research: designing surveys, analyzing both quantitative and qualitative data, and evaluating the strengths and limits of different forms of evidence. Students will develop projects that explain what sustains language learners and present their findings through clear, audience-ready reports, visualizations, and presentations.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Busting Language Myths
courses.description: "Women talk more than men! Texting means the end of literacy! The language you speak limits the thoughts you can think!" We often hear claims like these, but are they true? And what kind of information would show us the answer? This course examines current debates about language while developing skills in reading and interpreting research results, media reports, basic statistics, and data graphics.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Constructed Languages: Theory and Typology
courses.description: This course explores linguistic properties of constructed languages (conlangs). The course examines philosophical and creative motivations behind existing conlangs, and how their grammatical properties relate to those of natural languages. Students will explore and apply creative and analytical procedures used to create constructed language grammars.

source.text: LING 230. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 . | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Languages of Southeast Asia
courses.description: This course surveys languages spoken in Southeast Asia, an area rich in linguistic diversity, which is home to more than five distinct language families and well over 1,000 individual languages. Students will investigate the languages--in situ and in the diaspora--through the lens of descriptive linguistics, and will explore the social, cultural, and political aspects of languages in the region. This course is appropriate for students with an interest in linguistics or in Southeast Asia.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Special Topics in Linguistics
courses.description: In-depth treatment of a selected issue or topic in linguistics. Topic will vary with the instructor. Course may be taken more than once when the topic varies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language and Power
courses.description: This course provides an overview of language and power studies. Issues: sexist and sex-neutral language; languages of subcultures defined by gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity; hate speech; "politically correct" language.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Native Languages of the Americas
courses.description: This course is an introduction to languages indigenous to the Americas. The course touches on the linguistic structure and classification of Native American languages as well as on social issues. This version requires that the student learn intensively about the structure of a specific language, as well as its social and cultural context. Students may not receive credit for LING 561 after completing LING 303 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Discourse
courses.description: Focuses on the use of linguistic forms to express communicative intentions. How language is used for the purposes of persuasion, manipulation, irony, humor, poetry, propaganda, and attitudes.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Race against Time: Language Revitalization
courses.description: Students are introduced to the causes and contexts of language endangerment and the complex process of language revitalization. Topics to be covered include assessment of endangerment level, language and thought, language attitudes, bilingual education, and language planning. We will also consider a number of case studies of endangered languages.

source.text: LING 305. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 . | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Human Language and Animal Communication Systems
courses.description: Comparative study of human language alongside selected non-human communication systems. Anatomy, acoustics, combinatorial structure, innateness and acquisition, evolution. Sizable lab and field component.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Structure of African American English
courses.description: This course treats the structural properties of African American English. Students will learn to use sentence data to test hypotheses about language structure by investigating the phonology, syntax and semantics of African American English.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Hispanic Linguistics
courses.description: Introduction to the linguistic study of sound, meaning, grammatical form, dialectal and sociolinguistic variation, with a particular focus on modern Spanish and the languages of Spain and Latin America. Previously offered as SPAN/LING 377.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, SPAN 300 or SPAN 301; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: LING 360. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPAN 300 or SPAN 301 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-KNOWING. | SPAN 360 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Spanish Phonetics and Phonology
courses.description: Introduction to the description of sound systems with a focus on Spanish. Includes the study of the historical development of Spanish and its areal and social variation in Spain, Latin America, and the United States.

source.text: LING 376. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPAN 261 or SPAN 267 . | FC-KNOWING. | SPAN 376 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Group Mentored Research
courses.description: Permission of instructor. Students gain first-hand experience conducting research as part of a research group working together on a single project under the advisement of a faculty member. Topics will vary.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Language and Linguistics
courses.description: Seminar on a previously announced topic.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

source.text: LING 397. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPAN 300 or 301 . | SPAN 397 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Computational Linguistics
courses.description: An introduction to computational linguistics, a subfield of linguistics that explores natural language using computational tools and perspectives. We'll be using Python to analyze language structure at various levels, considering how computational approaches can help inform our understanding of natural language phonology, syntax, and semantics. We will also consider applications in natural language processing including, but not limited to, topics like segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, and parsing.

source.text: LING 401. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 . | FC-QUANT, FC-LAB.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Different Lives, Different Voices: Social Perspectives on Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: This seminar examines the relationship between language learning and diverse social contexts, focusing on how culture, identity, and community influence second language acquisition (SLA). Students will explore theoretical frameworks and empirical methods, with emphasis on quantitative and qualitative approaches. Through data collection, analysis, and hypothesis testing, we will assess the strengths and limitations of these methods in understanding SLA's social dynamics. Case studies and collaborative projects will highlight the lived experiences of diverse language learners, encouraging critical thinking and empathy. By course end, students will gain both theoretical insight and empirical research skills. Readings and class discussions in English.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Philosophy of Language
courses.description: At least two courses in philosophy other than PHIL 155 , including PHIL 345 , strongly recommended. A study of important contemporary contributions in philosophy of language. Topics include meaning, reference, and truth.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Research Methods in Phonetics and Laboratory Phonology
courses.description: Focuses on the practical skills required to carry out basic experiments in speech production or perception. Includes training in a general-purpose programming language (such as Perl) for automating repetitive tasks, experiment-control software, audio stimulus manufacture and editing, palatography, aerodynamic measurements, and other laboratory techniques relevant to student interests.

source.text: LING 422. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 200 , 520 , 523 , or SPHS 540 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Morphology
courses.description: Cross-linguistic investigation of internal word structure: inflection and derivation, word formation rules versus affixation, autosegmental morphology, morpholexical and morphophonemic rules, and the interaction of morphology with phonology and syntax. Previously offered as LING 527.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Bilingualism and Second-Language Acquisition
courses.description: This course covers theoretical issues in childhood simultaneous bilingualism, and child and adult second-language acquisition, under both naturalistic and classroom learning circumstances.

source.text: LING 428. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 . | FC-KNOWING, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Pragmatics: Understanding What People Really Mean
courses.description: How do we understand what people really mean, not just what they say? This course explores how speakers use language to convey meanings that go beyond literal words - through context, tone, inference, and shared knowledge. Students will examine topics such as implicature, presupposition, speech acts, and politeness, applying these concepts to real-world examples from everyday conversation, media, and cross-cultural communication. Designed for students curious about how language works in interaction, this course bridges linguistics, psychology, and social life.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Origin and Evolution of Human Language
courses.description: Recommended preparation, at least one higher-level core course in linguistics. Surveys current answers to such questions as, When and how did language first appear? What do other animal communication systems share with language? Do restricted linguistic systems (e. g., pidgins) preserve "fossils" of early human language?

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Philosophy of Language
courses.description: At least two courses in philosophy other than PHIL 155 , including PHIL 345 , strongly recommended. A study of important contemporary contributions in philosophy of language. Topics include meaning, reference, and truth.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Writing Systems: Past, Present, Future, Fictional
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the linguistic structure and historical development of the world's writing systems (e.g. Sumerian, Egyptian, Chinese, Greek, Semitic scripts, Indian abugidas, Olmec, Mayan, Incan), the methods for their decipherment and analysis, the cross-script generalizations that can be proposed through their comparative study, and the techniques for developing a new writing system for a previously unwritten language, as well as for inventing a language and writing system from scratch.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, LING 101; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: LING 458. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Making Sense of Big Data: Textual Analysis with R
courses.description: This course introduces students to the tools and quantitative methods needed to work with textual data in the age of big data. We will explore how large collections of text (corpora, digital archives, web-based sources, databases, etc.) can reveal meaningful patterns. Students will gain hands-on experience with the R programming language as they learn to clean and structure raw text, apply techniques for visualization and simple statistical analysis, and build models for categorization and interpretation.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Research Methods in Quantitative Language Science
courses.description: This course focuses on analytical and practical skills needed to test hypotheses using quantitative language data. Analytical topics include study design, statistical analysis, and interpreting results in the context of a hypothesis. Practical topics include tools and methods for working with "big'" language data, as well as statistical programming in R or a similar language. Students will design and carry out an original research study, analyze its results statistically, and present their findings orally and in writing.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, LING 460, STOR 320, or permission of the instructor.

source.text: LING 464. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 460 , STOR 320 , or permission of the instructor. | FC-QUANT, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Discourse and Dialogue in Ethnographic Research
courses.description: Study of cultural variation in styles of speaking applied to collection of ethnographic data. Talk as responsive social action and its role in the constitution of ethnic and gender identities.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Linguistics
courses.description: Directed readings on linguistic topics not covered in specific courses.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Internship in Linguistics
courses.description: Permission of instructor. This course allows students to integrate theoretical knowledge with practice through an internship experience in the field of linguistics. Students may work with businesses or organizations in the areas of computational linguistics, language documentation, education, publishing, or other related fields. Activities must be approved by faculty and supervised by a mentor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Individual Mentored Research
courses.description: Permission of instructor. Students carry out a research project of their own design under the direct supervision of a faculty mentor. This course is intended for advanced, motivated students who would like to pursue an in-depth research project within a single semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Independent Study in Linguistics
courses.description: LING 101 and additional coursework in linguistics strongly recommended. An intensive directed readings course or a mentored project; topic to be determined in consultation with the instructor. Permission of the director of undergraduate studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Structure of American Sign Language
courses.description: Introduces the linguistic structures of American Sign Language, including phonology, morphology, and syntax. Also covers gesture/homesign, sign language acquisition and language transfer.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Linguistic Phonetics
courses.description: Introduction to the general principles of linguistic phonetics; anatomy of vocal tract, physiology of speech production, universal phonetic theory. Practice in the recognition and transcription of speech sounds.

source.text: LING 520. | 3 Credits. | FC-NATSCI or FC-QUANT. | ANTH 520 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Experimental Phonetics and Laboratory Phonology
courses.description: This course relates linguistic theory to experimental findings. Students design and carry out experiments to test theoretical issues of current theoretical importance.

source.text: LING 522. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, LING 520 , and 200 or 523 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Phonological Theory I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. Introduction to the principles of modern generative phonology. Methods and theory of phonological analysis. Students may not receive credit for both LING 200 and LING 523 .

source.text: LING 523. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 520 , or SPHS 530 or 540 . | ANTH 523 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Phonological Theory II
courses.description: Intermediate phonological theory and analysis.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Historical and Comparative Linguistics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. Theories and methods of historical and comparative linguistics, with emphasis upon the Indo-European family. Students may not receive credit for both LING 202 and LING 525 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Second-Language Phonetics and Phonology
courses.description: Production, perception, and phonological patterns and processes in second-language learning and use. Effects of first-language transfer and universal linguistic factors. Seminar-style class based on primary literature.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Acquisition I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. One course in phonology or syntax recommended. Child language from a theoretical perspective. Topics include segmentation problems, acquisition of phonology, morphology and syntax, lexical acquisition, and language development in blind and deaf children and in bilinguals. Students may not receive credit for both LING 203 and LING 528 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Acquisition II
courses.description: This course focuses on the development of syntax in first-language acquisition in children. Topics will include parameter setting, null subjects, root infinitives, aspect, A-movement, binding theory, and control.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, LING 203 or 528, and LING 201 or 530.

source.text: LING 529. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, LING 203 or 528 , and LING 201 or 530 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Syntactic Theory I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. Methods and theory of grammatical analysis within the transformational generative framework. Special emphasis on analyzing syntactic and semantic structures of English. Students may not receive credit for both LING 201 and LING 530 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Syntactic Theory II
courses.description: Methods and theory of grammatical analysis, with special reference to transformational grammar.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Semantic Theory I
courses.description: Semantics as a part of linguistic theory: co- and disjoint reference among nominals, "crossover" phenomena, quantifier scope, lexical semantics, Montague grammar and compositional semantics, and explanatory universals in semantic theory.

source.text: LING 537. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 or 400. | FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Semantic Theory II
courses.description: A continuation of LING 537 (Semantic Theory I), this course prepares the student to read the formal semantic literature and to do original research in the field.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language of Time
courses.description: The representation of time and temporal relations in natural languages. Cross-linguistic study of tense and aspect distinctions, modality, temporal adverbials, temporal anaphora, and sequences of tenses.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Mathematical Linguistics
courses.description: Introduction to topics in logic, set theory, and modern algebra with emphasis on linguistic application. Automata theory and the formal theory of grammar with special reference to transformational grammars. No previous mathematics assumed.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Sociolinguistics
courses.description: Introduction to the study of language in relation to society; variation as it correlates with socioeconomic status, region, gender; the social motivation of change; language and equality; language maintenance, planning, shift.

source.text: LING 541. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 or 400. | ANTH 541 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Pidgins and Creoles
courses.description: Examination of the social contexts of language contact and their linguistic outcomes, with particular emphasis on the formation of pidgins and creoles. The course investigates the structural properties of these new contact languages and evaluates the conflicting theories that explain their genesis.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language in Politics
courses.description: Examines language as a political issue in the 19th and 20th centuries. Emphasis placed on American and British politics but attention to one other national context as well.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language and Mind
courses.description: This course explores the relationship between language and mind through the lenses of linguistics, cognitive psychology, and philosophy. Students will examine central debates about innateness, modularity, cognition, language evolution, and conceptual knowledge. We will also examine to what extent the current AI models can be said to model human cognition. By comparing and synthesizing disciplinary perspectives, students will learn how interdisciplinary approaches can provide a fuller understanding of complex questions about human cognition, meaning, and language.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, ENGL 213, LING 101, LING 400, PHIL 145, or PSYC 432; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

source.text: LING 545I. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, ENGL 213 , LING 101 , LING 400, PHIL 145 , or PSYC 432 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-KNOWING, INTERDISCI.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Theories of Second Language Learning
courses.description: What do we really know about how people learn a second language? This advanced seminar examines major theories of language learning, from behaviorist and innatist models to sociocultural and dynamic systems approaches. Students will critically evaluate research traditions, assess the cognitive and social factors that shape acquisition, and reflect on applications to pedagogy and policy. A central focus will be questioning what we think we know about language learning and how theories reshape those assumptions. Case studies from German and other world languages provide the foundation for discussion and application.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language Deficits and Cognition
courses.description: Survey of the linguistic properties associated with aphasia, autism, Williams syndrome, dyslexia, and schizophrenia. Emphasis on the implications of these conditions for theories of mind.

source.text: LING 547. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 or 400. | FC-KNOWING.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Indo-European: Phonology
courses.description: A survey of the phonological systems of the major Indo-European languages and their development from Proto-Indo-European.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Indo-European: Morphology
courses.description: Introduction to the major morphological categories in the Indo-European languages and their development from the proto-language.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Ancient Mayan Hieroglyphs
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the ancient scripts of pre-Columbian Mexico and Central America. It focuses on ancient Mayan hieroglyphs, describing their orthographic and linguistic structure, and highlighting methods for investigating the script using the Maya Hieroglyphic Database (5,000 inscriptions comprising 85,565 records). Students will write a research paper consisting of a linguistic and quantitative (descriptive, inferential statistical) analysis of a particular phenomenon of the script.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Mesoamerican Languages and Linguistics
courses.description: Surveys the basic characteristics that unify Mesoamerica as a cultural and linguistic area (e.g. sound systems, word order, color systems, diffused vocabulary, etc.), the basic sources of cultural and linguistic information available (e.g. ancient hieroglyphs, colonial manuscripts, contemporary documents, linguistic fieldwork), and the consequences of ancient and modern cross-cultural interaction.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Native Languages of the Americas
courses.description: This course explores the phonological and morphological structure of selected Amerindian languages indigenous to the Americas. Emphasis is on the linguistic analysis of original as well as published primary data.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Structure of Russian
courses.description: Examines Russian from the perspective of linguistic analysis. How do sounds, words, and sentences pattern in Russian? How do these compare with patterns in other languages? Also considers the influence of evidence from Russian on the development of linguistic theory.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, LING 101 or RUSS 102; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: LING 562. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, LING 101 or RUSS 102 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | RUSS 562 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Structure of Japanese
courses.description: Introductory linguistic description of modern Japanese. For students of linguistics with no knowledge of Japanese and students of Japanese with no knowledge of linguistics.

source.text: LING 563. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, JAPN 102 or LING 101 . | FC-KNOWING. | JAPN 563 .

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: History of the French Language
courses.description: The phonology, morphology, and syntax of French are traced from the Latin foundation to the present. Lectures, readings, discussions, and textual analysis. In English.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Historical Sociolinguistics
courses.description: This course studies the problem of language change by exploring the intersection of historical linguistics and sociolinguistics, addressing both the internal (linguistic, cognitive) and external (social, cultural) factors responsible for linguistic variation, linguistic maintenance, and linguistic change. The focus lies on the use of textual materials to understand the linguistic and sociocultural factors responsible for variation and change. Students will learn key methods and concepts from subfields such as historical linguistics, sociolinguistics, philology, paleography, and corpus linguistics. Both qualitative and quantitative approaches will be introduced, providing a well-rounded foundation for analyzing linguistic change and variation in historical data.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Spanish Semantics
courses.description: This course is an upper undergraduate/graduate-level introduction to the study of the meaning of words and sentences, with a focus on Spanish. It covers the following topics: truth-conditional theories of meaning, modality, quantification, reference, tense and aspect, Aktionsart. The course also addresses cross-linguistic data collection, e.g., field work and experimental methods.
